_comment: Linux x86_64 native self-build perf baseline. Captured 2026-05-06 (RFC-0063 Phase 1.3, R10-D3 closure). Companion to tools/perf_baseline.json (Windows). Pass via tools/check_perf_regression.sh --baseline tools/perf_baseline_linux.json on Linux runners. Update only after a measured intentional improvement; never to absorb a regression.

host.binary: bin/nucleor (ELF 64-bit LSB pie, x86-64-v1, for GNU/Linux 3.2.0)

_anti_compound_rule: Each Linux ship must come in at or below the ceilings above. Drift > 5% but < 10% requires investigation before shipping; never bump to absorb a regression.

_history.note: First-ever native Linux baseline (R10-D3 closure). Cold is ~2.4x the v0.8.317 Windows baseline (3.73s); hot is ~1.8x (0.26s). Gap is concentrated in the cold path — likely fopen / fork / exec / clang invocation overhead on Linux's standard glibc + ld-linux setup vs the v0.8.317 Windows tooling. Earmarked for RFC-0063 Phase 4 (PGO + LTO + per-arch SIMD). The hot-path delta is small enough that Linux production is viable today; the cold-path gap is the v1.0 perf target.
